name: decisions
scope: Four open decisions for the TARA threat catalog, October 2026 refresh. Proposals for human review only. No tracked file was modified; everything was written inside _staging/2026-10-refresh/.

deliberation.how: The quorum skill was invoked via the Skill tool and its protocol applied: six panelists did independent Phase-1 work without seeing each other's output, the supervisor built a claim pool and ran triage, two adversaries held opposed authentic positions with mandatory counter-proposals, then the supervisor synthesised. The panel ran as six parallel agents rather than the skill's internal multi-round converse loop.
panelists: Threat-taxonomy maintainer (MITRE ATT&CK / ATLAS content, CVSS SIG)
Product owner (device makers, notified bodies, regulators, API/SDK consumers)
Adversary 2, inclusionist outsider ('this gates on the wrong axis')
deliberation.confidence_rule: Confidence is the probability that the option is the right one, driven by evidence rather than by agreement among personas. Where the panel converged but nothing was verified, the score is capped and the basis says so.

close_calls.note: Within 0.15. Also the decision that changes nothing in this refresh: no full text of any candidate preprint was read, so every preprint-only item lands at EMERGING or below under either option.

decisions.question: What should count as DEMONSTRATED? The three proposed status changes that depend on whether dataset-only or simulation-only evidence qualifies.

premise_correction.claim_in_framing: The status values have no written definition.
premise_correction.finding: Incorrect. Definitions exist in three places and contradict each other.
premise_correction.verification: Read in the repo in this run.
evidence: datalake/README.md: CONFIRMED 'Demonstrated in real BCI systems or documented incidents'; DEMONSTRATED 'Proven in research/lab settings'; THEORETICAL 'Physically plausible, not yet demonstrated'; EMERGING 'Recently identified, under active research' (a recency label, not an evidence level); PLAUSIBLE 'Physically plausible, limited evidence'; SPECULATIVE 'Hypothetical, no direct evidence yet'.

src/lib/evidence-tiers.ts: maps CONFIRMED down to the 'demonstrated' group with the comment 'confirmed != peer-reviewed; best we can claim is demonstrated', maps EMERGING to 'speculative', and places simulation under THEORETICAL (theoretical_modeled).
src/pages/atlas/tara/[id].astro: maps CONFIRMED up to validated_replication and EMERGING to demonstrated_case.
src/lib/tara-projections.ts site legend: confirmed = 'real-world documented', demonstrated = 'lab-proven', theoretical = 'plausible', emerging = 'newly identified'.

blocking_finding.finding: Status is exported as a CVSS v4 exploit-maturity value, so the rubric cannot ship without the mapping change beside it.
blocking_finding.mechanism: datalake/scripts/transform-registry.py maps CONFIRMED -> E:A and DEMONSTRATED -> E:P.
blocking_finding.why_false: CVSS v4.0 defines E:A as 'Attacks targeting this vulnerability (attempted or successful) have been reported' and E:P as 'Proof-of-concept exploit code is publicly available'. No CONFIRMED entry in the registrar cites an in-the-wild attack on a neural device, so 27 machine-readable 'Attacked' claims are currently falsifiable from the CVSS specification itself.
blocking_finding.verification: VERIFIED (CVSS v4.0 specification text fetched and the quotations checked against the raw page; the mapping read in the repo).
blocking_finding.prior_art_in_repo: governance/outreach/DRBRYCE-QIF-CROSSREFERENCE.md already found that CONFIRMED 'conflates two different things ... the underlying phenomenon is documented in the literature and this has been demonstrated as an attack against a neural interface', and recommended two axes.

current_status_distribution.note: Six values in the data; src/lib/threat-data.ts Status type admits only four. 30 THEORETICAL entries have no sources at all. The DEMONSTRATED bucket holds hardware attacks, dataset ML attacks, re-applied general-ML papers (T0024), simulation-only (T0025), preprint-only (T0108) and one entry with zero sources (T0113).

options.label: D1-A
options.name: strict
options.description: DEMONSTRATED requires the attack run end to end against a physical device or live system; dataset-only results drop to EMERGING.
options.strongest_for: It is the only option under which the exported E:P is defensible for every DEMONSTRATED entry, and it matches what a device maker hears in the word 'demonstrated'.
options.strongest_against: When the decoder is the attacked system (membership inference, poisoning, model stealing), an offline attack on real recordings is the attack. D1-A systematically under-labels the ML half of the catalog and demotes T0016-T0019, among the best-sourced entries.
options.confidence_basis: established practice quoted in pack (ATLAS reserves 'Demonstrated' for a realistic system) plus judgement about the cost of under-labelling

options.label: D1-B
options.name: current leaning
options.description: Real hardware or real recordings both qualify; simulation-only stays EMERGING.
options.strongest_for: Cheapest to apply and it leaves the existing dataset-backed entries where they are.
options.strongest_against: It lets a dataset result claim the same label as Armengol-Urpi's over-the-air injection into three device classes and exports both as E:P. MITRE ATLAS draws the line the other way: 'Feasible - the technique has been shown to work in a research or academic setting'; 'Demonstrated - ... effective in a red team exercise or demonstration on a realistic AI-enabled system'. Under ATLAS's vocabulary, D1-B's DEMONSTRATED is Feasible. 'Simulation stays EMERGING' is also toothless while EMERGING means 'recently identified'.
options.confidence_basis: established practice quoted in pack contradicts it

options.label: D1-C
options.name: permissive
options.description: Any published empirical or simulation result is DEMONSTRATED.
options.strongest_for: Nothing to adjudicate; no curator judgement required.
options.strongest_against: It makes the word meaningless, conflicts with the project rule that a technique must distinguish what is possible today from what is projected, and raises the exported E:P count. No panelist supported it.
options.confidence_basis: established practice quoted in pack and the project's own rules

options.label: D1-D
options.name: two-part label
options.description: Keep four statuses, collapse PLAUSIBLE and SPECULATIVE into THEORETICAL, and require every entry to carry evidence_basis in {incident, hardware, participant, dataset, simulation, adjacent, review, none}, with the governing rule that the basis must match the attack surface the technique itself names.
options.strongest_for: It is the only option that separates the two questions the single ladder is being asked to answer (how strong is the evidence, and how close is it to a real device). That is the defect the in-repo audit identified and the present 43-entry DEMONSTRATED bucket demonstrates.
options.strongest_against: It is a schema change, not a relabel. The registrar has no field for the attack's evidence level (its only evidence_level is clinical), the refresh brief sends new fields to a proposed_fields note, and the TypeScript Status type admits four values while the data holds six. Until the site projection and transform-registry.py read the field, a reader still sees one word.
options.confidence_basis: established practice quoted from primary sources plus repo facts verified in this run; the dataset threshold inside it is judgement

decisions.recommendation_note: Adopt in the same release as a new exploit-maturity mapping. All six panelists chose D1-D, but the panel split on the threshold inside it: four allow dataset evidence to reach DEMONSTRATED when the model or data pipeline is the named surface, the strict adversary never allows it, and one allows it but would keep dataset entries out of the headline figure. The score reflects a verified diagnosis and a judgement-based threshold, not the unanimity.
decisions.confidence_basis: established practice quoted from primary sources plus facts verified in the repo in this run; the dataset threshold is judgement and the schema cost is real and unfunded
what_would_change_it: Evidence that API consumers, the site projection and transform-registry.py cannot read an added field without a breaking version: then D1-A is safer, because a single strict ladder beats a qualifier nobody sees.
Two curators independently assigning evidence_basis to the 43 DEMONSTRATED entries and disagreeing on more than 10%: the rubric would not be mechanically applicable and would need narrower wording.

Full text of a dataset-only evasion paper showing its perturbation survives a real analog front end (electrode impedance, filtering, artifact rejection): that would justify letting dataset evidence reach DEMONSTRATED for physical-surface techniques too.

exact_wording.paste_into: catalog documentation, and mirror into datalake/README.md replacing the current one-line table
exact_wording.preamble: A technique's status grades the evidence that an adversary's action produces the effect this technique names. Evidence that the underlying physical or biological phenomenon exists is not evidence of the attack. Every entry also carries an evidence_basis: one of incident, hardware, participant, dataset, simulation, adjacent (shown only on non-neural targets), review, or none. The basis records what was actually done; the status records how far that gets. The governing rule is that the basis must match the attack surface the technique names: for a technique whose surface is physical (signal acquisition, stimulation, tissue, radio, a worn or implanted device), only hardware or participant evidence can reach DEMONSTRATED; for a technique whose surface is a model or a data pipeline (inference, poisoning, evasion, model theft), dataset evidence on real neural recordings can reach DEMONSTRATED. An entry that describes more than one mechanism takes the status of its weakest mechanism, or is split.

levels.THEORETICAL: No source runs this attack against neural recordings, a neural model, neural tissue, or a device used to acquire or infer neural or cognitive state. The mechanism is argued from physics, from a review, from an analysis, or from a demonstration on a non-neural target (adjacent). Clinical and physiological evidence that the phenomenon exists, with no adversary in the loop, sits here. Entries whose citations do not resolve sit here with citation_unverified: true. A preprint can satisfy this level.
levels.EMERGING: At least one source with a resolved identifier runs this attack and reports an effect, but a DEMONSTRATED condition fails: the result is from simulation only (simulation); or the basis does not match the named surface (an offline result for a physical-surface technique); or the attacker's access or delivery path is assumed rather than achieved; or no reviewer has yet read a quantified success measure. A defence paper in which the attack is only assumed does not raise an entry above this level. A preprint can satisfy this level on its own, flagged preprint_only: true. EMERGING no longer means 'recently identified' - recency is not evidence.
levels.DEMONSTRATED: A citation-verified source runs this attack as named, against the surface this technique names, and reports a quantified success measure against a stated baseline, and a reviewer has read that measure and recorded whether it came from the abstract or the full text. Physical-surface techniques require hardware or participant; model- and data-pipeline techniques require dataset evidence on real neural recordings with the attacker's knowledge stated. Simulation never reaches this level. A preprint cannot be the sole basis; it can corroborate.
levels.CONFIRMED: Either (a) there is credible public reporting of this attack being used against a neural device outside research (evidence_basis: incident, recorded in a separate in_the_wild flag), or (b) the DEMONSTRATED criteria are met with hardware or participant basis by two groups sharing no authors, at least one of them peer-reviewed. Reproducing the phenomenon - a clinical TMS, tDCS or pharmacological protocol - does not qualify; reproducing the attack does. A preprint can never be the sole basis, and two preprints are not two groups for this purpose. No entry currently meets route (a).

exact_wording.exported_exploit_maturity: evidence_basis: incident exports CVSS E:A. DEMONSTRATED or CONFIRMED with hardware or participant basis and public artefacts exports E:P. Everything else exports E:U. Status alone never sets the exported metric.

decisions.question: Can a preprint support a status above EMERGING?

options.label: D2-A
options.name: no, cap at EMERGING
options.description: The current leaning. A preprint can never support a status above EMERGING.
options.strongest_for: It is already what the project's own rule enforces: .claude/rules/registrar.md requires DOI/PMID verification via the Crossref API before a technique is accepted as CONFIRMED or DEMONSTRATED, and arXiv DOIs return HTTP 404 at Crossref (verified in this run; they resolve at DataCite). D2-A therefore needs no rule change, which has real value after a fabricated-citation incident.
options.strongest_against: It ranks venue over evidence. CVSS v3.1 Report Confidence - the metric that exists for this question - grades reproducibility and independent confirmation and never mentions peer review. Cochrane s4.4.5 says preprints 'should also be considered a potentially relevant source of study evidence, particularly for emerging topics where little evidence exists' and that studies 'indicated that there was no compelling evidence that preprints provide results that are inconsistent with published articles'. Under D2-A a peer-reviewed defence paper that merely assumes an attack outranks a preprint reporting a measured hardware result.
options.confidence_basis: established practice quoted in pack, pointing against it; project rules pointing for it

options.label: D2-B
options.name: evidence type decides; peer review is a flag only
options.strongest_for: Maximally consistent with CVSS Report Confidence and with Cochrane: peer review is recorded, not gating.
options.strongest_against: arXiv's own terms state 'Material is not peer-reviewed by arXiv - the contents of arXiv submissions are wholly the responsibility of the submitter'. Several key 2026 sources here are single-author preprints. For a catalog read by device makers and regulators, with a fabricated-citation incident in its history, removing the venue floor entirely has the project's known failure mode. No panelist supported it.

options.label: D2-C
options.name: corroboration only
options.description: A preprint may be a supporting source at any level and the sole source at EMERGING or THEORETICAL, but never the sole basis above EMERGING.
options.strongest_for: It is the only option simultaneously compatible with the registrar's existing verification gate as written and with preprint inclusion as Cochrane recommends for emerging topics: the preprint still enters the catalog, the entry and the evidence list.
options.strongest_against: It still lets venue decide at the margin. A reproducible hardware preprint with public code is treated as weaker than a paywalled workshop paper whose full text nobody has read - which is the actual position of T0009's key source.
options.confidence_basis: established practice quoted in pack pointing both ways; the deciding factor is institutional, not epistemic

options.label: D2-D
options.name: conditional
options.description: A preprint alone may support DEMONSTRATED if the full text was read and artefacts (code or data) are public, flagged provisional and re-checked at each refresh.
options.strongest_for: It gates on the two things that predict whether a result holds (did someone read it; can anyone rerun it) rather than on venue, and it carries an explicit expiry.
options.strongest_against: The re-check duty has no owner, so provisional flags go stale - and the catalog has already shown it does not keep up its own checks (T0108 sits at DEMONSTRATED on two preprints; T0113 at DEMONSTRATED with no sources). It also requires amending the Crossref gate to accept DataCite, immediately after a fabricated-citation incident.
options.confidence_basis: established practice quoted in pack supports the principle; the operational precondition is missing

decisions.recommendation_note: Three panelists picked D2-D, two D2-C, one D2-A; all six agreed a preprint can never be the sole basis for CONFIRMED. D2-C is adopted over the plurality because it requires no change to a verification rule that exists because of a past failure, while still achieving what the D2-D camp wants in substance. The recommendation departing from the panel's preference order is flagged, not smoothed over, and is why this decision carries the lowest confidence of the four.
decisions.confidence_basis: established practice quoted from primary sources pointing in both directions (Cochrane s4.4.5 and CVSS v3.1 Report Confidence favour D2-D; the project's Crossref gate and arXiv's disclaimer favour D2-C); the choice between them is judgement about institutional risk tolerance
what_would_change_it: A working, owned refresh check that demonstrably demotes stale provisional entries: that alone would move this to D2-D.
The project amending its Crossref gate to accept DataCite for arXiv DOIs, plus a written 'public artefacts' test: the mechanical precondition for D2-D.
Evidence that BCI-security preprints change their results materially at publication more often than the Cochrane base rate: that would push toward D2-A.
A statement from MITRE ATLAS or ATT&CK on whether preprint-only evidence can reach their 'Demonstrated' level: not checked in this run, and the most relevant missing precedent.
decisions.exact_wording: Preprints. A preprint (arXiv, bioRxiv, medRxiv or similar) is admissible evidence and is recorded like any other source, with its identifier and the date it was read. It may be the sole source for an entry at THEORETICAL or EMERGING. It may not be the sole basis for DEMONSTRATED or CONFIRMED: at those levels at least one source must be peer-reviewed with an identifier that resolves at a registration agency (Crossref for journal and conference DOIs, DataCite for arXiv DOIs - note that an arXiv DOI returns 404 at Crossref and this does not mean the work does not exist). A preprint may corroborate, qualify or contradict a peer-reviewed source at any level, and a contradicting preprint must be recorded on the entry even when it does not change the status. Every entry whose evidence rests only on preprints carries preprint_only: true. When a preprint is later published, replace the identifier, re-read the relied-on result, and re-assess the status; results can change between versions.

decisions.question: Which of the 11 candidate techniques should be added, given the risk of inflating the headline count (165 -> 175)?

options.label: D3-A
options.name: add ten, hold R-084
options.strongest_for: Every named threat gets a queryable ID, a status and a score; nothing a device maker should know about is buried in prose. Five of the eleven name mechanisms the earlier in-repo audit listed as not covered (model stealing, MLOps registry compromise, federated integrity, air-gap channels, inferential HNDL).
options.strongest_against: Five of the ten would become top-level peers of entries that already cover them (R-081 and R-083 against T0019; R-082 against T0041; R-086 against T0024, whose own notes already name federated learning as an entry point; R-087 against T0043/T0046; R-088 is an umbrella over T0042, T0072, T0086 and T0094). ATT&CK ('sub-techniques are a more specific description of the adversarial behavior ... at a lower level than a technique') and CWE ('Variant Weakness ... more specific than a Base weakness') both keep narrower behaviours under a parent. Adding them as peers inflates a headline count on which three public artefacts already disagree, and creates two entries that score separately for one behaviour.
options.confidence_basis: established practice quoted in pack contradicts it

options.label: D3-B
options.name: add the distinct, fold the overlapping, hold the unverified
options.description: Four NEW, five FOLD, two HOLD. 165 -> 169.
options.strongest_for: It follows the taxonomy practice quoted above, and it gives the five folded results a home on the entry whose status they actually inform. R-083 in particular supplies T0109 - currently THEORETICAL with no primary source at all - with its first one.
options.strongest_against: The registrar schema has no parent, variant or sub-technique field, so a fold becomes free text in notes that the status logic, the counts, the KQL tables and API consumers cannot query. Folding is the under-labelling risk: real evidence becomes invisible.
options.confidence_basis: established practice quoted from primary sources plus repo facts verified in this run; the schema gap is inference

options.label: D3-C
options.name: primary empirical source only
options.description: Hold everything resting on the single review preprint.
options.strongest_for: The most conservative reading of the citation rules; nothing enters on one review.
options.strongest_against: A review is a legitimate basis for THEORETICAL under the D1 rubric, and this option would drop R-085 (model stealing), which a prior audit named as a real gap. Leaving a named threat out of a defensive catalog because only a survey describes it is the failure mode that harms the catalog's users rather than its critics. Rejected by the whole panel, including the strict adversary.
options.confidence_basis: judgement, weighing the cost of under-serving the reader

options.label: D3-D
options.name: add none until the rubric is adopted
options.strongest_against: The rubric and the additions can ship in one release, which is what the product owner wants anyway so each count is reconciled once. Pure delay; no support.

decisions.recommendation_note: Unanimous across all six panelists including both adversaries, and with identical per-card verdicts. The card-level agreement carries the score, not the headcount: the overlaps are checkable against the existing entries' own text, and the refresh agent that produced the cards had itself already proposed merging R-081, R-082 and R-087.
decisions.confidence_basis: established practice quoted from primary sources (ATT&CK sub-technique and CWE Variant definitions) plus repo facts verified in this run; the schema gap is inference
